import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1193

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1193](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1193)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
-/

open AdditiveCombinatorics Set

namespace Erdos1193

/--
Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ and let $g(n)$ be a non-decreasing function of $n$ which is always $>0$.

Is the lower density of
$$\{ n : 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=g(n)\}$$
always $0$?

The answer is trivially no to both questions: indeed if $A=\mathbb{N}$ (assuming $0\in\mathbb{N}$)
then $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n+1$ for all $n$. Presumably Erdős had some additional restrictions on either
$g$ or $A$ in mind, but these are not recorded in [Er80].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1193.parts.i : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ), Monotone g → (∀ n, 0 < g n) →
      {n : ℕ | sumRep A n = g n}.lowerDensity = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ and let $g(n)$ be a non-decreasing function of $n$ which is always $>0$.

Is the upper density of
$$\{ n : 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=g(n)\}$$
always $<c$ for some constant $c<1$?

The answer is trivially no to both questions: indeed if $A=\mathbb{N}$ (assuming $0\in\mathbb{N}$)
then $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n+1$ for all $n$. Presumably Erdős had some additional restrictions on either
$g$ or $A$ in mind, but these are not recorded in [Er80].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1193.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ c < (1 : ℝ), ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ), Monotone g → (∀ n, 0 < g n) →
      {n : ℕ | sumRep A n = g n}.upperDensity < c := by
  sorry

/--
Indeed if $A=\mathbb{N}$ (assuming $0\in\mathbb{N}$) then $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n+1$ for all $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1193.lean"]
theorem erdos_1193.variants.sumRep_univ (n : ℕ) : sumRep (Set.univ : Set ℕ) n = n + 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős writes the upper density can be positive, but he believes it is bounded away from $1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1193.variants.upper_density_pos :
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ), Monotone g ∧ (∀ n, 0 < g n) ∧
      0 < {n : ℕ | sumRep A n = g n}.upperDensity := by
  sorry

end Erdos1193

reformulations.difference: The cited external proof uses conv_ind, counting k in Finset.range (n + 1) such that k ∈ A and n - k ∈ A. The repository uses sumRep, counting ordered antidiagonal pairs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The map k ↦ (k, n - k) bijects the external count with {(a,b) ∈ A × A | a + b = n}; its inverse is first-coordinate projection. Membership in range (n + 1) ensures k ≤ n, so natural subtraction causes no discrepancy. Proved equality of the two counts for every A,n and the corresponding equivalence of the univ statements in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory, Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89–115, §3, especially pp. 98 and 100: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf
review.notes: No mathematical defects found in the four declarations. Erdős's survey states both density claims and the possibility of positive upper density without recording further restrictions. Thus the easy counterexample is faithful, not an accidental trivialization. Independently proved all four mathematical statements in scratch.lean using A = univ and g(n) = n + 1, whose matching set has both densities 1. Checked empty and singleton sets, n = 0, finite interval cardinalities, density normalization, positivity, and answer scope. The cited external proof also compiled unmodified; the checked proofs use only standard axioms, without sorryAx. Current community metadata records 1193 as solved (Lean), consistent with the file. Direct erdosproblems.com page/forum access was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the primary survey supplied the wording and the accessible community database supplied current status. Detailed checks are saved in /workspace/review/review-notes.md. No repository files were edited.
